messages:
sec-bot: [SECURITY ALERT] Suspicious auth tokens observed in staging logdrain to s3-external-bucket-xyz. Potential token fragments found. Tag: high
Harry: seeing it. paging SRE + security. assigning @Gina as on-call SRE, @Emma sec lead
Gina: on it. can someone paste the log snippet / bucket path? I'll spin up analyzer.
sec-bot: sample snippet attached (truncated): "auth_header: Bearer sk_live_abc123... user_id: 9876" — forwarded from staging/streams/2026-03-17/part-0003.log
Emma: confirm receipt. This looks like staging-facing debug logs containing token prefixes. Need containment + key rotation if any prod tokens leaked.
Ben: quick check — the s3 forwarder lambda was misconfigured to point to external bucket because of CI var override in repo infra-staging. Patching now.
Gina: action plan: 1) block external bucket access from our account; 2) revoke all staging service tokens; 3) search for any prod tokens in that bucket; 4) escalate rotation if found. Doing step 1 now.
Harry: I'm coordinating the incident bridge; creating zoom and pagerduty bridge. Link: zoom.g/incident/9200001111
Kate: CS — any customer-facing impact? None yet reported. We should prepare a brief internal customer notice in case.
Emma: I'll run a quick regex scan of the bucket for known prod token prefixes and user IDs. Frank can you run queries against token issue logs to detect reuse/external calls?
Frank: running queries now. Filtering by token prefix and anomalous outbound IPs. ETA 7m.
Gina: block applied: external-bucket access denied from our infra. Also set S3 ACLs to private and disabled bucket replication.
Ben: patch pushed to CI var; deploy in staging to prevent further forwards. Also rolling back last deploy to forwarder commit a2b3.
Carlos: tagging infra change and recording for audit. Adding temporary WAF rule to drop outbound to bucket host.
Frank: query results: 0 matches for prod token reuse in external bucket so far. Found 18 staging token fragments. No external calls observed using those tokens.
Emma: that's good but we need to assume tokens in staging are compromised. We'll revoke staging tokens and rotate any secrets used by staging jobs.
Gina: doing batch revoke of staging service tokens and restarting staging services. NOTE: this will interrupt staging CI jobs briefly.
Harry: on-call handoff: @Gina will remain primary until containment complete. If it's escalated, ping @Emma.
Julie: legal — do we need to notify regulators or anyone? If no customer PII, probably not, but keep me in the loop for final decision.
Kate: CS draft: "No customer production data affected. We are investigating and will update if impact changes." I'll prepare customer-safe language if needed.
Emma: timeline: analysis + rotation in 30-45m. If prod tokens found, we'll open a customer notification and full root cause report.
Gina: containment complete: forwarder disabled, tokens revoked, access blocked. Continuing forensic scan across buckets and internal logs.
Frank: additional check against egress logs: discovered 3 outbound PUTs to the external bucket from staging-forwarder within a 12h window. Files appear to be debug logs only.
Carlos: collecting hashes of the objects for integrity and raising takedown request with bucket owner.
sec-bot: system note — incident severity set to P2 due to leaked staging fragments, no prod confirmed.
Harry: summary for pager: P2, staging debug logs forwarded to external bucket; staging tokens rotated; no prod compromise detected; SRE+Sec continue forensic scan. @Kate @Julie looped.
Kate: added CS note to embargo until we confirm no customer impact. Prep message template ready.
Julie: legal ok to wait 24h for final if no escalation, else we'll follow notification playbook.
Gina: leaving detailed runbook notes in #incidents-docs. Closing immediate containment. Will post final forensic summary when scans complete.
Harry: thanks everyone. If you find additional anomalies, ping this thread and I'll reopen bridge.
sec-bot: incident updated: last action by Gina at 9200001449
